free_text.inst.v2.D8:
I read the plain-words page first, then went to the documented life. The general temperament line - 'responsive and changeable, guided a good deal by feeling' - is fine as far as it goes, and it isn't wrong about a performer who cried on stage and rewrote songs by instinct, but it's also a description that fits half of Hollywood; it doesn't earn its keep.

Where it actually goes wrong is on the page's own boldest claim. It flags itself as 'unusually positive about long illness and people who work against you' and invites the reader to test it there. Tested against the record, it fails both times. Long illness was not a strength in this life - vitiligo diagnosed and then revealed to Oprah Winfrey in 1993, lupus confirmed at autopsy, a scalp burned to the bone by pyrotechnics in 1984 that fed a real prescription-drug dependency, and a death in 2009 from acute propofol intoxication. That is not a matter that 'reads well.' People who work against you fares no better: a 1993 molestation allegation settled in civil court, a 2003 arrest and a 2005 criminal trial (acquitted on all fourteen counts, which the reading has no way to know and does deserve credit for not contradicting), tabloid coverage that never let up, and, by his own and biographers' accounts, a management and family structure around money that worked against him as often as for him. Two for two wrong on the specific claim the page staked itself on.

Where it lands closer: 'home, property and your mother' reading hard fits - Neverland went through a real foreclosure scare in 2008 before a late refinancing, and his relationship with his father genuinely was the hard, conflicted one of the pair while his mother was the steady one. And it correctly avoids saying anything decree-like about the death, which a cruder reading might not have resisted.

On marriage it says 'mixed'; the record is more clearly hard than mixed - two marriages, both ended within a few years, neither by most tellings a happy one. On money it says 'reads well' for income and 'reads hard' nowhere near property - true for the catalog and touring income, but it skips past a decade of serious, well-documented debt trouble that a plain reading of the man's finances would have to mention if it were going to talk about money at all.

Net: partly right on the family axis, wrong on its own flagged claim, silent on the drug dependency and the debt. I'd call it disagree rather than partly, because the failure isn't in the vague filler - it's in the two places the text chose to stick its neck out.

notes: Answered as Michael Jackson (b. 29 Aug 1958, Gary, Indiana; d. 25 Jun 2009, Los Angeles), from the documented public record, having read the plain-reading text first per the contaminated-arm protocol. Facts checked against Britannica, Wikipedia 'Michael Jackson' and 'Death of Michael Jackson', and the Health and appearance of Michael Jackson article (vitiligo revealed 1993 on Oprah; lupus confirmed at autopsy; propofol/benzodiazepine death 25 Jun 2009; marriages to Lisa Marie Presley 1994-1996 and Debbie Rowe 1996-1999; three children Prince, Paris, and Prince Michael II/'Blanket' via surrogate; 1993 Chandler allegation settled civil, no charges; 2003 arrest, 2005 acquittal on all 14 counts). Where the plain-reading text made a specific, falsifiable claim, the real life was allowed to overrule it: (1) it names itself unusually POSITIVE about long illness -> C2=opt2 (real difficulty) confidence 5, given vitiligo, lupus, the 1984 burn injury, and the addiction/death chain, and logged as plainly wrong in D1. (2) it names itself unusually POSITIVE about people who work against you -> C3=opt1 (real difficulty) confidence 5, given the two criminal investigations, the civil settlement, and the tabloid years; also D1. (3) its own flagged unusually-NEGATIVE claim about land/property does match the record (Neverland foreclosure scare, 2008) -> C4=opt1 confidence 4, kept as a genuine hit, not a contamination artifact, since the biography independently supports it. Elsewhere I let ambiguity stay ambiguous rather than resolve it toward the reading: C9 (sense of right conduct) is opt1 at only confidence 3 because he was acquitted on every count and no court ever found against him, but the allegations themselves and the settlement are real documented difficulty in that domain, so the honest answer sits closer to 'difficulty' without full confidence. C5 (vehicles) and C6 (ears/throat) are low-confidence opt1 answers because the record is simply thin there, not because either life-fact or the reading pulled hard. A36 has no honest answer - the question assumes a living respondent comparing the last few years to the six before, and Jackson died in 2009 - so 'same' is a placeholder flagged here rather than a real judgment. A16/A18 reflect that he ran his own production and publishing entities (MJJ Productions, the ATV/Sony-ATV catalog) rather than working for an employer. A23 is 'serious_past' rather than 'serious_now' because a 2008 refinancing and the March 2009 This Is It contract were underway at the time of his death, i.e. the crisis had a resolution path even though large debt remained. A33 'abroad' rests on the roughly year-long Bahrain residence in 2005-2006 after the trial, not on touring alone. D4 lists exactly the eight chapters specified as not shown (health_readout, medical, longevity, timeline, gochara, divisional, karmic, nichod); the plain-reading text's own house-by-house lists ('children and learning', 'marriage and partnerships', 'courage, and brothers and sisters', 'work and standing') were treated as covering those matters within plain_reading itself, so they are not separately flagged as skipped. D2 is left empty: nothing in the generic temperament paragraph or the vague house lists said anything specific enough to count as 'right and unguessable.'
